title: BK polyomavirus nephropathy

steps.tx: **BK polyomavirus** is a double-stranded circular DNA virus that resides latently in recipient and donor renal tubular epithelial and urothelial cells, reactivating under potent immunosuppression (particularly tacrolimus and MMF regimens). The image is decoy cells on urine cytology and BK virus nuclear inclusions.

steps.tx: **Decoy cells** are urothelial cells with characteristic ground-glass, enlarged basophilic intranuclear viral inclusion bodies, detectable in urine cytology during early BK viruria. One side is Decoy Cells (Urine), and the other side is Plasma BK PCR (> 10^4). Decoy cells are a sign of viruria, but plasma PCR is what guides the cut in immunosuppression.

steps.tx: **KDIGO** guidelines recommend routine screening for BK virus replication with plasma quantitative PCR monthly for the first 3 to 6 months post-transplant, then every 3 months until 12 months, and whenever serum creatinine unexplainedly rises. The paired value for Months 1 to 6 post-transplant is Plasma BK PCR monthly.

Immediate plasma BK PCR and biopsy

steps.tx: **Presumptive BK** polyomavirus nephropathy is diagnosed when plasma PCR threshold remains persistently >= 10^4 copies/mL (or >= 4.0 log10 copies/mL) for at least 3 weeks. The first step is Surveillance plasma BK PCR surveillance. The next step is Sustained viral load > 10,000 copies/mL (4.0 log10).
steps.say: Presumptive BK polyomavirus nephropathy is diagnosed when plasma PCR threshold remains persistently at least 10^4 copies/mL (or at least 4 point 0 log10 copies/mL) for at least 3 weeks. The first step is Surveillance plasma BK PCR surveillance. The next step is Sustained viral load greater than 10,000 copies/mL (4 point 0 log10).

steps.tx: Definitive diagnosis of BK polyomavirus nephropathy (**BKPyVN**) requires allograft biopsy demonstrating intranuclear viral inclusions, tubulitis, interstitial inflammation, and positive immunohistochemical nuclear staining for SV40 large T antigen. The image is renal allograft biopsy showing SV40 positive intranuclear staining. A positive SV40 stain is what proves the inflammation is BK nephropathy.
steps.say: Definitive diagnosis of BK polyomavirus nephropathy (BKPyVN) requires allograft biopsy demonstrating intranuclear viral inclusions, tubulitis, interstitial inflammation, and positive immunohistochemical nuclear staining for SV40 large T antigen. The image is renal allograft biopsy showing SV40 positive intranuclear staining. A positive SV40 stain is what proves the inflammation is BK nephropathy.

vis.alt: Renal allograft biopsy showing SV40 positive intranuclear staining
vis.caption: Immunohistochemical nuclear SV40 large T antigen positivity in viral tubulitis (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **Primary** cornerstone of therapy for BKPyVN is stepwise reduction of immunosuppression (reducing MMF by 50% or stopping it completely, followed by lowering calcineurin inhibitor trough targets by 25% to 50%). The first step is Presumptive or biopsy-proven BK nephropathy. The next step is Step 1: Reduce MMF dose by 50% or stop.

steps.tx: Adjunctive second-line therapies evaluated for refractory BK viremia include **leflunomide** (an active metabolite inhibitor of pyrimidine synthesis with antiviral properties), intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and cidofovir. The paired value for Leflunomide is Inhibits pyrimidine synthesis and viral capsid assembly. The paired value for Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) is Pooled donor neutralizing anti-BK antibodies.

steps.tx: Late complications of BK virus replication in the urinary tract include **ureteric stenosis**, ulceration, and obstruction secondary to dense viral-induced inflammation and scarring, as well as hemorrhagic cystitis. The first step is BK virus replication in donor ureteric epithelium. The next step is Transmural necrotic inflammation and ulceration.
